doc.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018

title: Closing thoughts on purpose and thanks
summary: Final reflections on serving others, Rowe's wrap-up and Lipsius's praise of his interviewing.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well, Fred, you’ve had an interesting life.

No it’s not. And I’ve enjoyed talking to you a lot, and sort of getting a feeling for the levels that you have been through. So you were curious why I called you for this, and it’s partly because you had an impact on me early on.
So I wish you continued good luck.

Thank you. The last thing I would just say for me, and I mentioned to a few students, this is just me so it’s not for anybody, just to think about. My only reason I think for playing now, and just being, is to just serve others. I don’t know if Charlie Parker was really doing that, or Coltrane. I don’t know and I’m not judging. And I tell my wife, I say I have no other reason to be living now. I mean I love — I’ve had a lot of experiences, gone through a lot of heavy stuff too with my wife, but I just feel my whole purpose — I’ve had a lot of gifts in my life, good parents, a lot of close friends in my life, some very painful things, but as long as I can take care of myself, is to encourage others to go on and whatever your dream is, in a good positive way, do it you know. Because a lot of people are going through a lot of pain and I know that feeling. So I’m there for them. Without being cocky about it. That’s just in my heart now. It wasn’t when I was younger. It was a strong purpose.
That’s a great note to wrap up on.

You are extremely easy. When I was watching Phil Woods to, the interview, I told my wife, I said, “He is great.” Like when I watched Johnny Carson years ago, as a comparison, he’s great, everybody loves him, loved him. But sometimes, maybe because he was a little nervous or on cocaine or something, he would interrupt people. And you don’t really do that. And sometimes if you don’t interrupt someone, and you give them something to say and you give them the right little seed you know, they might have a memory of something that they never shared before that might help someone else.
So I just thought you did a great job, the one time I watched you.
And you were prepared too. You know.
